sections.h2: Which Laurel County office takes in a recorded deed?
sections.html:
Laurel County deeds go to the Laurel County Clerk. The delinquent tax and records desk is in Room 203 at 101 S Main St, London, KY 40741, and the clerk's phone is (606) 864-5158. Under KRS 382.110 the filing belongs in the clerk's office for the county where the property sits, or where most of it sits when a tract crosses a line.

Sellers seldom handle the paper. The closing attorney or title agent brings the signed deed in, settles the charges at the counter and receives the recorded original back by mail. Recording is what puts a sale on the public record, because an unrecorded deed does not bind later purchasers or creditors who had no notice of it.

sections.h2: How big is Laurel County, and who buys homes there?
sections.html:
Laurel County was carved out on December 21, 1825 from Rockcastle, Clay, Knox and Whitley counties. It lies in the southeastern part of the state with London as the seat and largest city, and Corbin straddling into Whitley and Knox counties. Roughly 434 square miles of land include part of the Daniel Boone National Forest and part of Laurel River Lake. Alcohol sales are allowed only inside London city limits.

  • An estimated 63,746 people lived here in July 2025, 1.8 percent more than the 62,613 counted in 2020.
  • The county holds 27,063 housing units and 23,996 households, with owners living in 71.6 percent of the occupied ones (2020 to 2024 survey).
  • The middle home value is $159,500, and the median rent is $813 a month.
  • Median household income is $57,771, and the average commute takes 22.6 minutes.

Countywide retail sales reached about $1.68 billion in 2022 and health care receipts about $439 million, which shows London and Corbin acting as the job centers that draw buyers into town.

sections.h2: How must a deed show where the seller got the property?
sections.html:
A clerk may refuse a deed for a life estate or larger interest unless it points to the immediate source of the seller's title. KRS 382.110 sets the pattern for that reference.

  • Bought by recorded deed: cite the old deed's office, book, page and recording date.
  • Inherited, or acquired without a recorded writing: say how the title arrived and from whom.
  • Pieced together from more than one source: cite every source and mark which portion came from each.

Deeds signed by court commissioners or other court officers and instruments acknowledged before March 20, 1928 sit outside the rule. A mortgage holder that accepts a deed in lieu of foreclosure has 45 days after execution to file it. A seller who inherited should locate the probate papers well before closing so the deed language is right the first time.

sections.h2: What fees apply when you record a Laurel County deed?
sections.html:
The clerk's posted schedule lists minimums. A deed costs $50 for its first five pages and $3 for each page past that. A mortgage costs $80 and starts adding $3 per page after page thirty. Confirm at the counter whether any state charge is included in a quoted total before you cut a check.

On a routine sale the clerk's own charges are one short deed and one short release, about $96 together, which is small beside the title and lender costs.

sections.h2: How does the Kentucky deed transfer tax add up here?
sections.html:
Under KRS 142.050 the seller owes $0.50 on each $500 of declared value, and a leftover fragment of $500 counts as a whole unit. The clerk computes it and holds the deed until it is paid. A $200,000 price is 400 units, so the bill is $200. A sale at the county median of $159,500 is exactly 319 units, so $159.50.

When the deed is a gift or names only nominal money, the value used is what the land would bring on the open market. The clerk keeps five percent for collecting and sends the remainder to the county treasurer each quarter for the general fund. Several transfers owe nothing at all:

  • Foreclosure transfers and surrenders to a lender in place of foreclosure.
  • Deeds between spouses, or between ex-spouses as part of a divorce.
  • Nominal-price transfers from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild.
  • Deeds that only create or release a debt security, or fix an earlier recorded deed.
  • Tax sale deeds and partitions.

sections.h2: How can you search Laurel County land records?
sections.html:
The clerk steers researchers to eCCLIX, an online index that lets title searchers, surveyors and agents view and print recorded documents from a desk. People without an account can come to the courthouse and look at the records on site. Accounts come through the vendor, Software Management, by mail, fax or email, with card payment after an invoice arrives.

Title firms that send closings electronically use one of four e-recording services posted by the clerk: Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. The closing agent's software picks among them, so the seller has nothing to choose.

sections.h2: What tax bills should a Laurel County seller settle first?
sections.html:
Kentucky property tax is paid to the sheriff. The Laurel County Sheriff's Office at 1380 East Hwy 192, London, takes payment in person, by mail or at the front drop box, and takes cards inside. It is open weekdays and closed weekends, and the phone is 606-864-6600. Under KRS 134.015, paying in full by November 1 trims the bill by 2 percent, the printed amount applies from November 2 to year end, January adds a 5 percent penalty, and anything paid after January 31 carries 10 percent.

Bills still open when collection ends in April move to the clerk as certificates of delinquency, and interest and fees begin to stack up. The clerk's 2026 notice for outside buyers of those certificates set registration from August 17 to August 31 and asked for a deposit of 25 percent of each buyer's list value. Both dates are past. A title agent will ask for a payoff either way, so ask the sheriff for a bill history before the house goes on the market.

sections.h2: What should a Laurel County seller do before closing day?
sections.html:
• Pull the vesting deed and copy its book and page into the new deed.
  • Collect the sheriff's figures, current and past due, and ask the clerk about liens on record.
  • Ask each lender for a payoff statement, and plan who files the release.
  • Give the closing agent the buyer's in-care-of address for the next tax bill.
  • Decide whether a transfer tax exemption applies and gather its supporting facts.

Owners who want no showings or repairs can get a direct offer, and the filing and tax steps above are the same whichever buyer signs.

faqs.q: Where is a London, Kentucky house deed filed?
faqs.a: With the Laurel County Clerk at 101 S Main St in London. That one office serves London and the Laurel County side of Corbin, since the deed goes where the land lies.

faqs.q: What does recording a Laurel County deed cost at minimum?
faqs.a: Fifty dollars buys five pages, and each extra page adds $3. A mortgage starts at $80 and a mortgage release at $46.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when a Kentucky house sells?
faqs.a: The seller. KRS 142.050 puts it on the grantor named in the deed, at fifty cents per $500 of value, and the clerk collects it when the deed is presented.

faqs.q: Can the public view Laurel County deeds for free?
faqs.a: Yes, in the clerk's office. Viewing from home through eCCLIX needs a paid account.

faqs.q: When must a lender file a deed in lieu of foreclosure?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after signing is the limit, and the filing goes to the clerk in the property's county. KRS 142.050 also leaves that deed free of transfer tax.
